maintenance.page.title: Maintenance
maintenance.page.empty: No printer is registered yet, so there is nothing to maintain.
maintenance.page.printerHoursHint: Type what the printer's own display shows, such as 14d 7h. The printer's counter is the whole, the server's count is the part it saw.
maintenance.page.confirmDoneTitle: Did you really do this maintenance?
maintenance.page.confirmDoneBody: The counter starts again at the printer's current hours. Only press yes once the work is done.
maintenance.cards.due.heading: Maintenance due
maintenance.cards.due.none: Nothing is due. Every task is inside its interval.
maintenance.page.templateNote: One schedule for every printer. Change an interval here and every printer's task of that name follows; its hours and Done stay on the printer's Maintenance tab.
maintenance.tab.toolsHint: An indication, not a measurement: the print's length split by the filament each tool pushed in the prints whose G-code this module could still read. Retractions count towards the tool that made them.
maintenance.tab.confirmResetBody: The tool's counter starts again at zero. The printer's own counter is not touched.
maintenance.page.setsHint: One schedule per printer. A printer follows the schedule its model brings until you point it at another one on its page; a copy can be edited, a shipped schedule only switched off.
maintenance.page.introWhat: Maintenance counts the print hours of every printer and reminds you when a task is due. Every printer keeps its own counter and its own Done marks; this page decides which tasks it has.
maintenance.page.introHow: A printer follows the schedule its model brings until you pick another one in the Schedule field on its Maintenance tab. The shipped schedules can be switched off, and their intervals can only be changed in a copy; duplicate one, edit the copy, and assign it.
maintenance.page.introValues: The shipped intervals are the ones in the Prusa Knowledge Base article on the CORE One, and each schedule links to the article it was read from. Another model's article may give different numbers, so check it before you rely on them, and put your own values in a copy you make here.
maintenance.page.introNew: Name of the new schedule creates your own: give it a name, pick the printer model it is meant for, press New schedule, then open it and add the tasks you want, in print hours or in days. A schedule that counts days is how you ask for a check every three months no matter how much the printer runs.
maintenance.tab.setHint: Which schedule this printer follows. A shipped schedule holds the Prusa Knowledge Base intervals; a copy of it is where you change them.
maintenance.page.abrasiveHint: Carbon and glass filled filaments wear most nozzles down fast. Brass, stainless steel and plated copper are printed in bold italic because they are not made for them; hardened steel, bimetal, silicon carbide, tungsten carbide and ruby last.
maintenance.manual.title: Maintenance manual
maintenance.manual.what: It counts the print hours of every printer and tells you when a maintenance task is due. The hours come from the server's print history; the value the printer shows is typed in once, and from then on both counters move with every print.
maintenance.manual.counters: Every printer carries two figures, and they are kept in step:
maintenance.manual.countersStep1: Server hours: everything this server has printed since the printer was set up.
maintenance.manual.countersStep2: Display value: the number on the printer. Type it in once. On my printer it read 14d 7h; written as 343 h it is the same figure, and the module reads both the same way.
maintenance.manual.countersStep3: From then on both move with every finished print. When they drift apart, correct the display value again.
maintenance.manual.sets: A set is a named plan with several lines: a task, an interval, optionally a material. Every printer follows exactly one set.
maintenance.manual.setsShipped: Eight sets ship with the module: seven for a model (Core One, Core One L, HT90, XL, MK4S, MK3, M3) and one for any printer. Each names the Prusa Knowledge Base article it came from.
maintenance.manual.setsCopy: A shipped set cannot be edited or deleted. Duplicate it, change the copy, assign that one.
maintenance.manual.setsAssign: Assign it on the printer's tab, in the Schedule field. The printer keeps its own hours and its Done marks; only the lines around them change.
maintenance.manual.setsOff: Switching one off works too: it leaves the list but stays in the module.
maintenance.manual.intervals: A line counts either in print hours or in days. Hours suit parts that wear with use. Days suit a calendar check, such as the linear rail once a quarter, even when the printer runs little. Done asks first and anchors the next interval at the printer's current hours.
maintenance.manual.nozzles: A nozzle line chooses its material, and the interval follows the life of that material:
maintenance.manual.tools: Each printer's tab also shows how many hours ran through every tool. The module reads the G-code of finished prints, .gcode and .bgcode, deflate, heatshrink and MeatPack included, and splits the print's length by the filament each tool pushed. The figure is an indication, not a measurement, and the tab says so. After a nozzle change, Start over at 0 resets that tool alone; the printer's counter stays where it is. Time is kept to the second: on an INDX print a nozzle sometimes works for forty seconds, and counted in whole minutes that would look as if nothing had been recorded at all. Not out of pedantry - well, a little.
maintenance.manual.status: Every task carries a state, and the state follows the share of its interval that is used:
maintenance.manual.statusOk: green: time left, the task is not marked.
maintenance.manual.statusSoon: yellow: the threshold is reached, 90 percent by default. Plan it, no need to panic.
maintenance.manual.statusDue: red: the interval is over. The task sits at the top and on the event bus.
maintenance.manual.card: Maintenance due lists each printer's tasks with a coloured dot and the share used. Red first, then yellow, then green. If a printer has no name, its model stands in.
maintenance.manual.where: The shipped sets come from the Prusa Knowledge Base, each line linking its article, and the nozzle lives are from there too. When in doubt, check a number at the source instead of trusting the module.
maintenance.manual.check1: No counter moves: is the printer the same one the server knows? A printer set up anew starts at zero.
maintenance.manual.check2: Tool hours are missing: the G-code has to sit in the server's storage as a finished print, and the module needs read_storage.
maintenance.manual.check3: Everything green although you printed: display value and server hours apart? Type the display value in again.
